business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa — unitary national jurisdiction (Johannesburg/Gauteng and national CIPC registry; no sub-state incorporation)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended, and Companies Regulations 2011. Key sections: s.1 (definitions), s.8(2) (private company), s.13 (incorporation), s.14 (registration), s.19 (legal personality), s.40 (consideration for shares), s.66 (board), s.69 (directors), s.86 (company secretary), s.70 (registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (form CoR 14.1), together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and supporting documents as prescribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up share capital is required for a private company (Pty) Ltd in South Africa. Shares must be issued for adequate consideration, and any discount on shares is prohibited. There is no escrow or banked capital requirement; the company may commence business immediately after obtaining its registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the Memorandum of Incorporation executed by the initial members and incorporators is adopted as the company's constituent document; (2) that the share subscription agreements presented to the board are ratified, and that the initial directors named in the MOI are appointed effective immediately; (3) that the company's registered office be constituted at the address stated in the Notice of Incorporation and that all statutory correspondence may be served there; (4) that the chairperson, company secretary, and chief financial officer be appointed to manage statutory filing and tax compliance; (5) that the directors be authorized to open bank accounts with licensed financial institutions and to execute all applications with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission and the South African Revenue Service; and (6) that these resolutions be implemented without further formality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File form CoR 9.1 electronically via the CIPC online portal. Provide three proposed names in order of preference. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee (approximately ZAR 50) using the e-channel payment option. If the name is reserved, obtain the name reservation number and validity period (36 months). If no name is reserved, the company may be incorporated using its future registration number.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the incorporator or authorized agent
Power of attorney if submitted by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected, CIPC will provide a written reason. Submit an alternative name or, if supportable, request a reconsideration or appeal to the CIPC Name Tribunal within 60 business days. Ensure that no names conflict with existing trademarks or registered companies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the MOI and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC-authorised attorney or company secretarial practitioner; notarial execution may be required depending on provisions in the MOI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation in conformity with the Companies Act and the company's intended governance structure. Complete the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and the schedule to CoR 14.1. Have the incorporators and initial directors execute the documents. If the MOI contains constraints or shareholder authorisation provisions, ensure that the notary public authenticates signatures. Prepare a signed consent-to-act form for each director.
required_dossiers: Schedule to CoR 14.1 (attachment of directors and share capital)
Copy of identity documents of all incorporators and directors
If a name reservation was used, the name reservation number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOI fails to meet the statutory requirements, CIPC will issue a compliance query. Revise and resubmit the affected pages within 20 business days. Engage an attorney to amend the MOI so that it does not contradict the Act, and ensure all signature blocks are properly dated and witnessed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Payment to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the CIPC e-Services platform. Select the Company Registration icon and attach the completed CoR 14.1, Schedule, and MOI as scanned PDF files. Populate the required data fields (company name, capital structure, director details). Pay the prescribed incorporation fee of approximately ZAR 125 using Visa/Mastercard or e-channel. Retain the electronic payment receipt and submission reference.
required_dossiers: Scanned copy of Schedule to CoR 14.1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, CIPC will issue an error report with specific grounds. Amend the relevant form by logging back into e-Services, correct the deficiency, and resubmit. If payment failed, retry the payment process. Escalate unresolved matters to the CIPC contact centre or the Registrar's office for a formal ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful verification, CIPC will issue the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and the company's unique registration number (e.g., 2025/123456/07). Download the certificate from the e-Services portal. Verify that all details (company name, directors, share count) are correct. Store the certificate securely as the founding legal evidence of corporate existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or not issued due to background verification, contact the CIPC helpdesk. If the certificate contains errors, submit a Notice of Amendment (CoR 14.2) and request a corrected certificate. For loss of certificate, request a duplicate via form CoR 14.4.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the South African Revenue Service (SARS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax using SARS form IT/COR 14.2. Trigger is mandatory within 21 days after incorporation. Register for Value-Added Tax (VAT) if projected annual turnover exceeds the R1 million compulsory threshold (or R50,000 voluntary). Register for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF), and Skills Development Levy (SDL) once the first employee is engaged. Complete bank account verification via SARS with the company's banking details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects the registration due to information mismatches, verify the taxpayer reference and resubmit the corrected form. If the company profile is not linked to eFiling, submit a request for a tax compliance status and use the SARS branch counter. If failure is due to non-verification of banking details, obtain an updated Fica-confirmed bank letter and reattach.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Records and Bank Account Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board and licensed South African banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to approve the issuance of shares and record the resolutions in writing. Establish the statutory records (share register, directors' register, minutes book, and accounting records). Appoint an independent auditor or exempt the company from audit via shareholder consent (s.30(2)(c)). Open a corporate bank account at a licensed bank by presenting the registration certificate, MOI, board resolution, and Fica documents.
required_dossiers: Fica documents (identity, proof of address, source of funds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application, remedy by providing additional Fica documentation and a certified board resolution for account administration. If the independent reviewer appointment is challenged by shareholders, call a shareholder meeting and elect a new reviewer. Any rectification of records must be filed with CIPC if a change of registered office or directors is needed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Planning and Development Department (local zoning or land-use authority) – applicable only if the company occupies physical premises; otherwise no industrial licensing authority is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Operating Licence under municipal business regulations – not required for remote software and online screen-share services; an administrative Certificate of Compliance (COC) for the leased office may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software development and remote telemetry are not listed activities under EIA Regulations Listing Notices 1, 2, or 3 (2014). No full Environmental Impact Report or Basic Assessment is triggered for a purely virtual office operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to a software-only operation. If a small physical office is used, comply with municipal wastewater discharge limits, general waste management regulations (2013) for office waste, and the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) regime for end-of-life electronic equipment; any e-waste must be handed to a registered recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate or Fire Clearance from the relevant local Fire Protection Service for the registered office premises; Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993) compliance including a general workplace safety file; certificate of electrical compliance (COC) for the leased office; and for a remote workforce, a documented home-office risk assessment is recommended but no physical clearance is mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at www.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African private company (Pty) Ltd must incorporate under the Companies Act 2008 and thereafter register for income tax via SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using the SARS Registration, Amendments and Verification (RAV) process. The company must submit its Memorandum of Incorporation, certificate of incorporation, directors'/officers' identification, registered office and postal address, bank confirmation, and financial details. SARS issues a separate income tax reference number; PAYE/UIF/SDL registration is required if the company becomes an employer; VAT registration is required once taxable turnover exceeds R1 million per 12-month rolling period, with voluntary registration possible once taxable turnover exceeds R50,000 per 12-month period. A foreign company deriving South African-source income or having a permanent establishment must register for income tax under the same RAV process and may be required to register for VAT if it supplies taxable electronic services into South Africa above the R1 million threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not have a check-the-box classification regime. Comparable statutory elections under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 include the controlled foreign company apportionment election under section 9D(2A), the prepayment allowance election under section 24C, the research and development allowance election under section 11D, and the VAT grouping election under section 21(1A) of the VAT Act 89 of 1991 allowing two or more entities to be treated as a single vendor. Hybrid mismatch adjustments are applied under sections 8F and 8FA for hybrid debt and hybrid instruments, with no elective opt-out for covered instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 compulsory annual taxable turnover; voluntary threshold R50,000 annual taxable turnover; foreign suppliers of electronic services must register if the aggregate value of taxable supplies to South African residents exceeds R1,000,000 in any 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or government API stamping requirement for B2B e-invoices. VAT vendors must issue tax invoices satisfying section 20 of the VAT Act within 21 days of the supply, retain complete digital records under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, and submit VAT returns and payment via SARS eFiling. SARS has promoted e-invoicing and standard business reporting, but no digital clearance gateway is compulsory as of the current legislative position.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% VAT under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act when supplied to a non-resident and exported from South Africa within the prescribed timeframe, with the supplier retaining documentary proof of export. Services, including remote screen-share and IoT telemetry software, qualify for 0% under section 11(2)(l) when supplied to a non-resident who is absent from South Africa, provided the services are not supplied directly to a person in South Africa and are not attributable to movable property or land in South Africa. The supplier must obtain a written declaratory confirmation from the recipient and safeguard evidence of export/offshore supply for audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500/XML lodged through the SARS Customs clearance process)
Commercial invoice with full exporter, consignee, value and destination particulars
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/authorised-dealer evidence showing receipt of foreign currency proceeds
VAT 177 declaration or equivalent export voucher where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow the zero-rating, raise an additional VAT assessment, impose interest, and apply an understatement penalty under section 222/223 of the Tax Administration Act of up to 200% of the shortfall where the failure is due to intentional tax evasion or substantial impermissible avoidance. Deliberate submission of false export evidence is a criminal offence under VAT Act section 58 and Customs and Excise Act provisions, carrying a potential fine and imprisonment. Exchange control contraventions for failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may trigger administrative penalties and further SARS audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) — Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), administering exchange control under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations promulgated thereunder (R.1111 of 1963, as amended), with designated authorised dealer banks (commercial banks) executing day-to-day controls and reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including software licence fees, telemetry subscription revenue, royalties, professional fees and dividend profit remittances, via an authorised dealer without SARB prior approval, subject to FICA-driven KYC verification and the documentary requirements of the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers. Capital-account inflows are open to non-resident investors subscribing for shares or extending shareholder loans, but require formal FDI reporting to FinSurv (Form DBR filed through the authorised dealer within 30 days of receipt) and are prohibited where a prohibited 'loop structure' — a South African-resident owned foreign entity reinvesting into South Africa — is present. Dividend remittances to foreign shareholders require: (i) certification of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 solvency and liquidity test; (ii) withholding of 20% dividends tax or a reduced treaty rate supported by SARS income-tax-residence certification; and (iii) a board resolution and underlying financial statements evidencing distributable reserves. South Africa's FATF grey-listing (February 2023 to October 2025) elevated enhanced due diligence on cross-border flows; following removal from the grey list, banks still apply heightened beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds scrutiny but no material convertibility denial is expected for bona fide ISIC 6201 software-export receipts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Proceeds from service exports, including remote-desktop-software licensing and unattended-IoT-telemetry subscription fees, must be repatriated to South Africa and credited to the resident exporter's account with an authorised dealer within 180 days of the invoice date, in accordance with the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers and related Exchange Control Circulars. No mandatory conversion to ZAR is imposed; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a Foreign Exchange Account (FEA) or flexible FEA, but any conversion into ZAR is executed through the authorised dealer at prevailing market rates. Each inward receipt must be traceable to the underlying export invoice and reported under the applicable services-export economic measurement code. If the 180-day repatriation deadline cannot be met, the authorised dealer must flag the overdue receivable and the exporter must apply to FinSurv for an extension or a 'no-objection' ruling before the expiry of the statutory period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (primary ZAR) + Foreign Exchange Account (FEA) for USD/ZAR liquidity; Capital Escrow Account available for staged FDI subscriptions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Business Online treasury platform; FEA overlay for export proceeds; Capital Escrow Account for initial equity injection
Operational Account (ZAR) + FEA; trade finance and commercial LC desking for outbound procurement
Operational Account + FEA; dedicated corporate FX desk for forward exchange contracts
Operational Account (premium structured treasury) + FEA; suited to scale-up tech balance sheets

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — Conditionally viable as a secondary rail only. An offshore digital EMI or fintech treasury provider (e.g., Wise Platform, Payoneer, Airwallex) cannot independently operate as a deposit-taking bank or settlement participant in South Africa without SARB recognition under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998; it must route local settlement through a licensed authorised dealer. The target payment rails (Stripe and Paddle, operating as Merchant of Record / payment facilitators) are permissible for collecting overseas SaaS and IOT-telemetry subscription fees and paying out the ZA (Pty) Ltd's funds by FEA wire transfer, but they are not substitutes for a domestic corporate bank account. The EMI channel cannot execute SARB FDI reporting (EM code filings), cannot maintain a SWIFT-settled ZAR account with FEA compliant aggregation, cannot provide onshore ZAR-denominated forward exchange contracts, and would trigger FICA business-relationship objections if used as the sole liquidity hub for foreign-director funding. Recommended architecture: the principal treasury anchor must be a tier-1 authorised dealer bank, with Stripe and Paddle retained as collection disbursement channels whose net proceeds are swept into the domestic operational account under the 180-day repatriation rule.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA Directive 5 of 2022 permits supervised non-face-to-face account opening where the accountable institution applies enhanced due diligence, and leading South African banks have operational remote onboarding with video KYC and liveness verification. In practice, the major banks still require at least one director, shareholder or formally mandated representative to appear physically — or to have their identity and authority notarially certified by a recognised bank or compliance officer — before the operative account mandate and beneficial-ownership disclosure are accepted. For a fully remote team of non-resident directors, the workable approach is either: (i) appoint a local authorised signatory under a board-approved power of attorney to attend the branch and execute the mandate, or (ii) complete the bank's structured video interview with the Relationship Manager and Compliance and Financial Crime team, submitting certified passport copies, certified proof of residential address, the CIPC registration certificate, MOI, beneficial-ownership register and a board resolution resolving the account opening. Foreign directors should budget for a mandatory pre-credit compliance interview focused on source of funds, anticipated cross-border transaction flows and the ISIC 6201 software subscription model before the account is activated for international settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity arising from non-resident shareholders holding the South African (Pty) Ltd through intermediate offshore holding vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC beneficial-ownership register extract (Companies Act section 56), comprising full legal and natural-person BO identification together with percentage holdings; certified copy of the Memorandum of Incorporation and complete shareholders' register; corporate-entity chart of each intermediate vehicle with continental legalisation; certified passports of every natural person holding 25% or more; board resolution confirming the absence of bearer shares, nominee structures or undisclosed trusts; and notarised corporate standing documents (certificate of incorporation, register of directors) for each non-resident holding entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty for the initial inbound equity injection, particularly where the subscription derives from accumulated overseas SaaS revenue, crypto-asset realisation or intra-group claim conversion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve to twenty-four months of audited or full management bank statements for the remitting shareholder; executed purchase and sale agreements, annual accounts and platform payout statements evidencing realised proceeds; tax residence certificate of the funding shareholder and the relevant SARS or foreign-tax filing history; a sworn forensic accountancy verification report mapping the source of assets to the subscription amount; and the Form DBR (FDI declaration) annexure submitted through the authorised dealer to SARB FinSurv within 30 days of the receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Historic FATF grey-list exposure and any current linkage to higher-risk jurisdictions in the counterparty base, director domiciles or funding institution chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete counterparty due-diligence file containing KYC packets, operating licences, identity documents and commercial standing of each client; underlying service agreements, invoices and telemetry/service-delivery records evidencing genuine ISIC 6201 trade; SWIFT instruction histories with correct purpose codes; sanctions and politically-exposed-person screening results from a reputable screening provider (e.g., LexisNexis or World-Check); and a compliance attestation confirming that all proceeds arise exclusively from remote-desktop-access software and unattended-machine IoT-telemetry subscriptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified operational substance of a remote software company with no physical office lease and no South African payroll, raising shell-entity and tax-residency red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SARS income-tax registration and tax-clearance PIN; MOI evidence that board decision-making and central management and control are situated in South Africa; IP ownership or development agreements and technology-hosting contracts (AWS or Azure) proving local economic substance; telecommunications and data-centre service invoices; audited projections demonstrating receipts flowing into the South African bank account; and an independent accountant's modern-substance opinion distinguishing the entity from a shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual early-life cross-border payment pattern, such as high-value outbound disbursements to foreign suppliers or an offshore parent shortly after account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved board minutes for each disbursement; supplier invoices, purchase orders, delivery confirmations and distribution agreements; a treasury policy evidencing the FX-risk matrix and hedging intent; the authorised-dealer EM code record supporting each payment; and proof of the commercial rationale for the underlying procurement of software development services, cloud infrastructure or licensing fees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident share subscription or shareholder-loan funding must enter South Africa exclusively through an authorised dealer bank via a compliant SWIFT chain: MT103 single-customer credit for direct remittances or MT202 COV for bank-to-bank cover, with the SWIFT remittance narrative expressly stating 'Share subscription — ZA_PTY_LTD — FDI equity capital' and carrying the SARB Economic Measurement (EM) purpose code for inward direct-investment equity (EM 3840) as applied by the receiving bank. The authorised dealer will demand: (i) a board resolution approving the allotment of shares or the loan facility; (ii) an updated MOI and shareholders' register or the CIPC share-allotment return (CM26); (iii) full source-of-funds evidence from the remitting shareholder; (iv) a signed Form DBR (foreign-direct-investment declaration) transmitted to SARB FinSurv within 30 days of the receipt; and (v) FICA-compliant identity and beneficial-ownership verification. No SARB prior approval is required for bona fide FDI below the applicable alert thresholds, but the transaction is rejected where a prohibited loop structure exists. Operational service-export proceeds from Stripe and Paddle settlements are routed under the computer-and-information-services services-export EM code with the 180-day repatriation obligation, and each inbound payout is matched to the underlying telemetry-subscription invoice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements are executed through the authorised dealer using SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfers, each supported by the underlying invoice, the applicable destination EM code and FICA-compliant commercial documentation retained for SARS and SARB audit. Where a foreign supplier or distribution counterparty requires documentary security, an irrevocable sight commercial letter of credit governed by UCP 600 (or eUCP for electronic records) is the permissible clearing rail, although software subscriptions and cloud-infrastructure payments are ordinarily settled by clean wire with the corresponding FX forward cover. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders follow the regulated remittance path: solvency-and-liquidity certificate under the Companies Act, 20% dividends tax withheld (or treaty-reduced rate), board resolution, and an authorised-dealer payment instruction using the income and distributions EM category. All outbound disbursements are subject to the SARB requirement that they be effected through the formal banking system, never through informal value-transfer channels, and the entity must maintain the treasury dossier evidencing real commercial or capital-account substance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Fixed-dated forward exchange contracts (FECs) executed with the authorised dealer, fully documented against underlying USD/ZAR telemetry and licensing receivables.
Option-dated (window) forward exchange contracts matching the variable monthly payout timing of Stripe and Paddle subscription settlements.
Participating and plain-vanilla FX options purchased from the authorised dealer, hedging downside beyond the budget rate on large dividend or supplier disbursements.
Cross-currency swaps covering long-term USD-denominated shareholder loans or material foreign vendor contracts.
Exchange-traded USD/ZAR currency futures and options admitted to trade on the JSE interest-rate and currency derivatives market.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on ZAR initiated only through the authorised dealer corridor or an approved international treasury hub, strictly restricted to hedging genuine underlying telemetry-software export exposures and never used for speculative positioning.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return including Beneficial Ownership confirmation (annual return fee band ZAR 950 based on turnover between R1m and R10m)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation; for a 29 February financial year end, the due date is always recalculated from the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs 10% of the annual return fee for each commenced month of delay; two or more consecutive outstanding annual returns trigger delinquency status and CIPC administrative strike-off; reinstatement requires payment of outstanding fees plus an additional CIPC reinstatement charge

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SARS Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) for the registered financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the company financial year end (customarily 28/29 February); provisional taxpayers must submit first and second six-monthly provisional returns (IRP6) with a top-up payment at the year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty of 10% of assessed tax per commenced month of non-filing (capped); understatement penalty of 10% to 100% of the shortfall depending on conduct; interest at the SARS prescribed rate (repo rate plus 7 percentage points, approximately 14.5% per annum); directors can be held personally liable for tax debts in cases of reckless non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) with Financial Accountability Supplement (FAS) to CIPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (audited AFS must be lodged only when Public Interest Score is 350 or more; otherwise AFS remain at the registered office for CIPC and SARS inspection); SARS for tax record purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Board must prepare AFS within 6 months after financial year end under Companies Act section 30; the FAS is submitted simultaneously with the CIPC annual return within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare AFS or submit FAS is an offence under the Companies Act; directors may be subject to administrative fines, director disqualification, or a court-ordered mandatory audit; breach risks penalty of up to ZAR 1 million for the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: POPIA Information Officer and Deputy Information Officer annual registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on 30 June, covering the period from the date of commencement of business or date of appointment of the Information Officer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register the Information Officer is an offence under POPIA; administrative fines up to ZAR 10 million per incident and potential criminal liability with imprisonment up to 10 years for serious breach of the Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: EMP501 Annual PAYE/UIF/SDL Reconciliation (mandatory only if employing staff)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final annual reconciliation due by 31 May following the 1 March to 28/29 February tax year; interim reconciliation by 31 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalties of 10% to 15% of the unreturned PAYE amount; monthly administrative non-compliance penalties for employers; interest at the SARS prescribed rate (repo rate plus 7 percentage points) on both late remittances and late declarations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required when the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more, or when the company is a public or state-owned company, or when the Memorandum of Incorporation or a shareholder resolution directs an audit. A PIS between 100 and 349 requires an independent review unless shareholders direct a full audit. A PIS below 100 requires no audit or review absent direction. PIS is calculated as 1 point per employee, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party liabilities, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of turnover, and 1 point per individual holding a beneficial interest in the company
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is mandatory for public interest entities; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for private (Pty) Ltd companies; no South African local GAAP remains in force; statutory books and financial statements are prepared in ZAR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Beneficial Ownership Filing (BOF) must be submitted to CIPC annually at the same time as the annual return, confirming every beneficial owner of any shareholding including indirect, nominee, or effective control interests under Companies Act section 50 as amended by the General Laws Amendment Act 22 of 2022. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership during the year must be recorded in the Beneficial Ownership Register and reflected in a revised BOF filing; the annual confirmation must include full legal name, identity or passport number, nationality, residential address, and extent of interest of each beneficial owner
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board and Shareholder Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: ZAR 6,000 - ZAR 25,000 per annum (approximately USD 330 - 1,370), depending on CIPC agent, company secretarial services, and annual return administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: ZAR 40,000 - ZAR 150,000 (approximately USD 2,200 - 8,200) for a full IFRS for SMEs audit; independent review typically ZAR 15,000 - ZAR 60,000 (approximately USD 830 - 3,300)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (standard rate for South African companies for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; previously 28%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday is available. Preferential deductions include the 150% deduction for qualifying research and development expenditure under section 11D of the Income Tax Act, the 100% capital allowance on assets used directly in production, and the section 12H learnership allowance. The reduced progressive rates for South African Small Business Corporations apply only if shareholding and turnover thresholds are satisfied.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (assessed losses are carried forward until set off against future taxable income, subject to continuity-of-trade and change-in-shareholding anti-avoidance rules)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Income Tax Return for Companies) submitted electronically via the SARS eFiling portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Provisional tax returns (IRP6) are due six months after the start of the year of assessment and at the end of that year, with the second provisional payment due within six months after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The completed ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the company's year of assessment. For a company with a 31 March year-end, the filing deadline is the immediately following 31 March.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and income tax reference number of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are not disclosed on this line; any non-resident director details must be captured in the supplementary IT14 director schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total South African source gross turnover, including subscription receipts from remote desktop screen-share software, unattended machine telemetry and IoT support services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Turnover attributable to foreign services is reportable to SARS only if derived through a South African permanent establishment; foreign-source income not connected with a South African PE is excluded from South African taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Portion of prior assessed loss available and set off against current taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to a non-resident unless the non-resident operates through a South African branch whose PE has an assessed loss carried forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at the 27% statutory rate on taxable income after allowable deductions, exemptions, rebates and the set-off of assessed losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with a South African PE must allocate profits attributable to the PE and pay normal tax on those profits at 27%; no withholding tax applies to branch notional interest or deemed distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: SARS may raise a deemed assessment and administrative non-compliance penalties: a fixed periodic penalty of up to ZAR 16,000 per month of non-compliance and a percentage-based penalty of 10% per month on assessed tax, capped at 35%. Prescribed interest runs on unpaid taxes. Responsible directors may be held personally liable for PAYE, VAT and other third-party taxes under section 166 of the Tax Administration Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% dividend withholding tax charged on the gross amount of any dividend paid by a South African company to a non-resident beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a double taxation agreement, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver a complete DTD Declaration (including tax residence details) to the South African company acting as withholding agent before the dividend payment is made. SARS may require a tax residence certificate from the foreign revenue authority. The company must retain the declaration, submit the dividends tax return (DTR02), and remit the corrected withholding amount to SARS within 30 days after the dividend becomes payable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 15% for royalties and 15% for interest paid to non-residents. Applicable DTA rates commonly reduce royalties and interest to 0–10% depending on the treaty. Exemptions apply to interest on foreign-listed public debt and certain government borrowings.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Compulsory Local File and Master File preparation and retention apply when the value of international connected-party transactions exceeds ZAR 50,000,000 per year of assessment. South African multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least ZAR 10 billion must additionally prepare Country-by-Country reports.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime in the style of the UAE, but genuine economic activity is required through the place-of-effective-management test, CFC legislation, transfer-pricing rules and the general anti-avoidance rule under section 103(1) of the Income Tax Act. A remote screen-sharing or IoT company must evidence real personnel, board decision-making, and operational delivery in South Africa to avoid recharacterisation of its cross-border arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omission from the ITR14 of invoiced amounts derived from South African remote desktop subscriptions, attribution of local revenue to shell companies in no-tax jurisdictions, or deliberate understatement of infotech service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under sections 234 and 235 of the Tax Administration Act; an understatement penalty of 200% of the shortfall plus interest; asset seizure and preservation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax through the responsible-person provisions of the Tax Administration Act, face criminal sentences of up to five years, and may be prohibited from leaving the country while under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A South African (Pty) Ltd registered solely as an IP-holding vehicle with no employees, local office, decision-making, bank account, or service capability while profits from software sales are shifted to offshore related entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of intercompany payments and recharacterisation under section 31 (transfer pricing) and section 103(1) (GAAR), 200% penalty on the adjustment, non-recognition of the deemed intra-group transactions, and possible deregistration under the Companies Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil for reckless trading under section 22 of the Companies Act; directors are jointly and severally liable for tax liabilities and may be disqualified from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file beneficial ownership returns with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), maintaining bearer shares, omitting FATCA disclosures for U.S. persons, or failing to appoint a FICA compliance officer with complete client identity verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FICA administrative penalties of up to ZAR 10 million; CIPC may issue a non-compliance notice and a delinquency order; SARS may impose a 10% monthly administrative penalty for non-filing of required tax-related information; money laundering offences attract imprisonment up to 10 years under POCA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a delinquent company may be personally liable for its debts while trading, and are individually subject to criminal sanction and travel bans when the non-compliance conceals criminal proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Profit Repatriation / Dividends Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising a dividend as an interest-free loan to offshore shareholders, paying amounts overseas without settling dividends tax, or claiming treaty relief without a valid DTD declaration and tax residence certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax recouped from the company, interest and penalties, non-deductibility of the distribution, deemed-dividend treatment under sections 31 and 64E, and an understatement penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors are personally liable under section 156 of the Tax Administration Act for the dividends tax not withheld and remitted; SARS may issue attachment notices to banks; continued non-compliance constitutes a criminal offence with imprisonment.
